title: Commit
description: A single commit in an auru-pm-v1 project history. Standalone on purpose: the canonical encoding is a hashing contract, not an HTTP one, so an SDK needs this shape without pulling in openapi.yaml. See 'Canonical commit encoding' in auru-pm-v1.md.

id.description: BLAKE3 of the RFC 8785 canonical encoding of every other field.

parents.description: Length is the commit shape: 0 root, 1 normal, 2 merge.

message.description: One-line summary entered at Save Version time.

auru_version.description: Version of the client that produced the commit.

format_version.description: Snapshot schema version at commit time, so a reader knows whether a snapshot needs migration before restore.

metadata.description: Blob holding this commit's ProjectInfo — a few kilobytes describing tempo, key, tracks and plugins, so a client can show what a version is without fetching the ~7 MB snapshot. Absent on older commits and on formats the writer could not summarize; a reader that finds it missing falls back to the snapshot.

origin.description: Why the commit was made when it was not a person pressing Save Version. Absent on every explicit save, so older commits keep their ids; a reader may treat absence as a saved version.

contentHash.description: BLAKE3 in canonical `blake3:<64 lowercase hex>` form.

safeInteger.description: RFC 8785 numbers are IEEE-754 binary64, so every integer on a commit must stay inside +/- (2^53 - 1). Outside it, two conformant implementations derive different ids from the same commit.

snapshot.description: Blob holding the canonical project JSON for this commit.

samples.description: Blob listing (path, hash) pairs the project depends on. Samples download lazily, so this is the cheap 'what do I need before playback' probe.

authorIdentity.description: Captured inline rather than looked up, so history renders without a live provider connection and attribution survives a user leaving a workspace.
